caption: The drawing consists of architectural-style line illustrations of a walnut armchair, shown in both front and side elevations. The illustration is rendered in black ink on a yellowed, beige background, with all lines and text appearing in black. The front view of the chair depicts a high, gently arched and curved backrest with a decorative crest, a shaped splat in the center, cabriole legs, outwardly curved arms with scroll ends, a rounded seat, side supports, and feet with subtle curves. Beside the front view, the side elevation shows the depth and shaping of the arm, the curve of the back, the seat, and the profile of the legs and feet. The top right part of the side elevation includes one arm rendered separately. Numerous measurements, labeled in inches, are marked with dashed lines and numerals indicating specific dimensions for various parts of the chair. A separate diagram at the bottom center shows the seat's top view as a semi-circular shape labeled with its width. In the lower right, a title block contains printed information including the title, description, identification numbers, and the date ("May 19th 1936") along with the name "Alfred Nason." The overall composition is technical, with an emphasis on accurate proportions and specifications, and is devoid of shading or color beyond the background and ink.
title: Arm Chair
